title: Nationwide launches 1% deposit mortgage for first-time buyers
summary:
Nationwide Building Society has introduced a 99% loan-to-value mortgage product, enabling first-time buyers to purchase property with a 1% deposit. Industry professionals have raised concerns about negative equity risks amid declining house prices.

The post Nationwide launches 1% deposit mortgage for first-time buyers appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: LRG to acquire JLL’s UK high street estate agency business
summary:
LRG has agreed to acquire JLL's UK high street estate agency business in a deal scheduled to complete on 1st February 2027, bringing nine residential offices and 144 staff into its network. The transaction will increase LRG's footprint to more than 100 residential estate agency offices across Greater London.

title: Second home numbers fall 9.7% in England’s coastal hotspots
summary:
England's second home count has dropped by approximately 20,000 properties since 2024, with the steepest declines in coastal areas where councils charge double council tax. House prices in the nine most affected areas have fallen 8.8% from their 2022 peak, while rental costs continue to rise.

title: Independent estate agents face mounting pressures in 2027
summary:
Independent estate and letting agents are entering 2027 facing simultaneous pressures across landlord management, sales pipelines, and business valuations. The Bank of England's recent interest rate rise coincides with mortgage rates at approximately 6% and agreed sales down 7% year-on-year.

title: AI conveyancing firm launches pre-offer property tool
summary:
Conveyd has launched Property Preview, a tool providing prospective buyers with access to legal property information before submitting an offer. The AI-powered service addresses the UK market issue where legal documentation remains inaccessible until after offer acceptance.

title: Rent arrears reach £9,000 as court delays double landlord losses
summary:
Landlords in England are owed an average of nearly £9,000 in unpaid rent by the time arrears cases reach court hearings, according to new research. The analysis reveals that rental arrears typically double during the legal process, with three-month delays between serving notice and court hearings allowing debts to escalate from £4,398 to approximately £8,796.

title: Property agents cannot evade investigations by switching schemes
summary:
The Property Ombudsman has clarified that estate agents cannot avoid responsibility for ongoing investigations by transferring between redress schemes. The statement follows revelations about complaint handling involving a Glasgow-based property firm and £277,725 in ordered redress payments.

The post Property agents cannot evade investigations by switching schemes appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: UK property auction sales decline 14.6% in October 2026
summary:
Residential property auction sales in the UK fell 14.6% year-on-year in October 2026, with 2,285 lots sold compared with 2,677 in the same month last year. Despite the monthly decline, rolling 12-month figures show continued growth, with lots sold increasing 7.8% to 26,955 and total revenue reaching £4.86 billion.

title: Property tech firms focus on augmenting staff roles with AI
summary:
Property technology companies are positioning artificial intelligence tools as workforce enhancers rather than replacements, according to industry data and case studies from the lettings sector. Research from Alto's 2026 Agency Trends Report indicates that one-third of estate agents describe themselves as nervous or unsure about AI adoption.

title: Later life mortgage lending reaches £6.6bn in Q3 2026
summary:
Mortgage lending to borrowers aged over 55 reached £6.6 billion in the third quarter of 2026, representing a 2.2% increase compared to the same period in 2025. The banking trade body reported 38,800 new loans were advanced to this age group during Q3, down 2% year-on-year.
